narrative.text:
NARRATIVE:

Facts of Encounter/ Arrest: On May 18, 2017, Unites States Border Patrol agents (BPAs) from the [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] Michigan Station were conducting [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] in Escanaba, Michigan. At approximately 12:30 p.m., BPAs [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] and [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] observed an Escanaba Police officer conduct a traffic stop near the intersection of [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] BPAs then pulled behind the officer to assist with the stop if requested.

The officer from the Escanaba Police Department approached the BPAs, stated that he had pulled the vehicle over for improper display of plate and provided the BPAs with biographical information pertaining to the six occupants of the vehicle. The driver of the vehicle [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] was issued a citation for Improper Display of Plate and Driving without a license. The vehicle was towed and stored by the Escanaba Police Department. The information identified four of the subjects as being from Guatemala, one subject as being from Mexico and one subject as being from El Salvador. This information was relayed to LBPA [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] who conducted checks on the subjects indicating the following: one had been ordered removed, one had been voluntarily returned to Mexico seven times, three individuals were negative in the systems, and the last subject was in status. At that time, BPAs [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] and [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] approached the vehicle. BPA [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] identified himself as a Border Patrol agent and asked all subjects whether or not they had any immigration documents to be or remain in the United States legally. Five subjects stated that they did not have any immigration documents. BPA [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] then asked all subjects individually if they were in the country legally or illegally. All subjects stated that they were in the United States illegally. The subjects who admitted to being in the country illegally were placed under arrest and transported to the Escanaba Police Department until BPAs who could transport them to [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] Station for processing arrived. At approximately 3:20 PM, BPAs left Escanaba, Michigan enroute to the Border Patrol Station in [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] Michigan. Once at the station, [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] fingerprints and photograph were captured and entered into the [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] systems. Additional records checks were conducted through Detroit Sector Radio. The results were the following:

IMMIGRATION HISTORY:

No immigration history.

ENTRY:

[REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] claims to have illegally entered the United States in Laredo around 2015. He claims to have swam the river to cross the border. He then travelled to Houston Texas where he has lived ever since.

INADMISSIBLILITY/DEPORTABLILTY:

212(a)(6)(A)(i) of the Immigration and Nationality Act, as amended, in that you are an alien present in the United States without being admitted or paroled, or who arrived in the United States at any time or place other than as designated by the Attorney General.

CRIMINAL HISTORY:

No known criminal history.

DISPOSITION:

[REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] received a Warrant of Arrest/ Notice to Appear. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] and his property were transported to the [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] County Jail pending his removal proceedings. As per the new priorities established by the Executive Order, [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] was not given a bond because he violated Section 212(a)(6)(A)(i) of the Immigration and Nationality Act. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] claimed and appeared to be in good health. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] was notified of his right to contact the Consulate office of his native [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] country. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] contacted the Guatemalan Consulate at 9:40 P.M. Witnessed by Agent [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] was given a list of free legal services. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] claimed to have fear of returning to Guatemala because of violence.
